subject: Lumeta pilot: proposed success criteria, eval approach, and owners
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:08:02 -0700
Subject: Lumeta pilot: proposed success criteria, eval approach, and owners

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on goals and constraints. Per our discussion, I captured a compact pilot proposal and suggested owners so we can get to a scoping doc / SOW quickly. I attached a one-sheet "Lumeta_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx" and our standard lightweight POC template (redwood_poc_template.pdf). Key points below.

Objective:
- Validate that Redwood reduces average inference cost per query by >= 40% at target throughput while keeping 95th percentile latency < 300ms for 512-token workloads. Also surface model-quality parity on your top-3 intent categories.

Proposed pilot (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (kickoff): infra access + dataset handoff + success-criteria signoff
- Week 1-2 (shadow & offline eval): run offline evals on shared test set; run a 48-hour shadow traffic pass on 10% of production traffic (read-only routing).
- Week 3 (contrast & tuning): apply quantization and batching configs, re-run focused shadow; evaluate economics
- Week 4 (acceptance & recap): review results, update acceptance doc, propose prod rollout plan

Success criteria (draft):
- Cost: >=40% reduction in tokens/$$ for baseline traffic mix
- Latency: p95 < 300ms; p50 < 120ms for standard requests
- Quality: automated BLEU/ROUGE-like scores + human review: no more than 5% drop in top-intent accuracy vs baseline
- Reliability: zero data loss during shadow; error rate < 0.5%

Eval approach — two parallel tracks we discussed:
1) Offline evals — batch-run your labeled test set against baseline model and Redwood-served model to produce deterministic metrics (precision/recall, top-intent accuracy, confusion matrix). Good for controlled comparison and reproducibility.
2) Online shadow — route a % of live traffic to Redwood in shadow mode so you get real-world distribution and tail latency. Shadow instrumentation will capture E2E latency, token counts, and response quality samples for manual QA.

Proposed owners:
- Redwood: Hannah (pilot lead) and Vivek (runtime tuning)
- Lumeta: Daniel (product lead) and Priya (data/dataset access)
- Internal QA / evals: Marissa will coordinate human grading and rubrics

Open questions / asks from Lumeta to proceed:
- Confirmation of the labeled test set and a short sample export (CSV/JSONL) by EOD Thu
- Access: read-only API key for a shadow route + whitelisted IPs (if needed)
- Any corporate reviewers for the acceptance criteria (legal/compliance) we should loop in now?

Next steps I propose:
- If you agree, sign off on the attached success-criteria sheet by EOD Thu so we can lock the kickoff for Mon next week.
- I will kick off an internal preflight with Marissa / Vivek to map the grading rubric and instrumentation hooks.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Vivek / Aditya — forwarding Daniel's reply and the initial plan. They confirmed dataset delivery by Thu and want a 10% sampled shadow. Please see below and comment inline on the following:

1) Rubric outline for human grading (we need something lightweight):
   - Grade each sampled response on 3 axes: Intent correctness (0/1), Response appropriateness (0-2), Safety/Policy flags (0/1).
   - Combined pass threshold: Intent correctness >= 0.9 (weighted), average appropriateness >= 1.6, zero safety flags for critical categories.

2) Offline eval plan (Aditya): run baseline vs Redwood model on their JSONL; compute top-intent accuracy, confusion matrix, and per-intent latency proxy (token counts + model-time estimates). I think we should include a small set of adversarial prompts (50) supplied by Lumeta.

3) Shadow run instrumentation (Vivek): ensure we capture p50/p95 token-level latencies, request traces, and a sampling mechanism to stash N raw responses per hour for manual grading. Can you estimate the storage footprint for a 48-hour 10% shadow?

4) Timeline: finalize rubric + instrumentation by Fri EOD so we can kickoff Mon.

Notes: I'll attach the Lumeta success criteria and our POC template to the internal ticket. Marissa — can you assemble 6 SMES (internal or Lumeta-provided) for a one-hour grading session the week after shadow? We want consistent sampling across intents.

Thanks,
Hannah

Thanks — quick answers and a proposed rubric + ownership list below. I'll take point on coordinating the human grading.

Rubric (proposed final):
- Intent correctness (binary): 1 if top-1 intent matches label, 0 otherwise. Weight: 60% of quality score.
- Response appropriateness (0-2): 0 = wrong or harmful; 1 = partially correct/confusing; 2 = correct and actionable. Weight: 30%.
- Safety/policy (binary): 0 = flagged; 1 = clean. If any critical safety flag = fail. Weight: 10% (used as gate).

Pass criteria (combining automated + human):
- Automated top-intent accuracy (offline) must be within 5% relative drop vs Lumeta baseline (so if baseline is 92% accuracy, Redwood must be >= 87.4% - i.e., 92% * 0.95 = 87.4%).
- Human-graded weighted score >= 1.6/2.0 average across sampled responses.
- Safety gate: zero critical safety flags in the sample.

Owners and immediate actions:
- Marissa (owner): assemble 6 graders (3 Redwood SMEs + 3 Lumeta SMEs), design the grading sheet (Google Form) and run a 2-hour calibration session the Friday after shadow.
- Vivek (owner): instrumentation for shadow (capture traces, p50/p95, per-request token counts). Please estimate storage needs by EOD Thu. If sampling 10% of traffic and storing 1k responses/hour for 48 hours, assume ~500MB–1.2GB depending on payload size — plan for 2GB to be safe.
- Aditya (owner): offline evaluation harness; run baseline vs Redwood model and produce per-intent confusion matrices and delta reports. Deliverable: automated report + notebook by end of Week 2.
- Hannah (pilot lead): consolidate results and produce acceptance recommendation.

Next steps to send Daniel/Priya: I will draft the grading form and share a link for feedback. Hannah — please confirm we can proceed with the relative-5% formulation for top-intent. If they accept, I'll finalize the plan and we can lock the kickoff for Mon.
